predecessors.name: Union of Burma (Myanmar)
predecessors.text: Pegu Region: the first shots were fired at Paukkongyi, Pegu Region, on 2 April 1948, and the leadership's jungle headquarters stood 'in the Pegu Yoma near Paukkaung'

successors.name: Wa State
successors.text: the Wa hills round Panghsang (Pangkham), a 90 km circle cut to Shan State: 'In the late 1960s, the CPB arrived in the Wa hills of northern Burma'

successors.name: Myanmar National Democratic Alliance Army
successors.text: the Hopang-Kokang hills, a 60 km circle at Hopang cut to Shan State: after entering in January 1968 the CPB gained 'control over the Kokang substate'; Hopang is the nearest place with coordinates on…

ledger.x: 1948: the Communist Party of Burma begins its revolt on 2 April.
1948: the insurgency against the new Union of Burma begins ('the CPB fired the first shots of the conflict in Paukkongyi, Pegu Region' on 2 April 1948).
1968: the CPB's Northeast Command takes the Chinese frontier hills.
1968: the north-eastern front opens; the Northeast Command fought the junta in Shan State, 'where the CPB lost 500 people over 100+ battles'.
1975: with the Pegu Yoma base gone the contest in Pegu Region ends.
1975: the headquarters is at Panghsang by November 1978 and 'remained there until 1989'; the page does not date the move, so 1975 is a bridging judgment.
1989: the Wa troops at Panghsang break away.
1989: the CPB collapses at Panghsang on 16-17 April; the breakaway armies sign ceasefires.

1989: the Communist Party of Burma's armed state ends when 'a group of mutineers stormed the party headquarters in Panghsang' on 16 April 1989; its north-east passes to the Wa State, the Kokang MNDAA and the Mong La NDAA.

wars.name: Internal conflict in Myanmar (CPB insurgency)
wars.outcome: The Pegu Yoma base was destroyed in 1975; the Northeast Command broke up in the mutiny of 12 March to 17 April 1989 and its successors signed ceasefires.

certainty.note: Guerrilla bases with no recorded boundary; the Northeast Command's lines are the researcher's circles round Panghsang and Hopang.
